reviews.text:
All in all, it’s great. The features available do help me keep biz organized and maintain good comms w/customers. 

However, there are some issues that cause headaches and take time to learn so you’re prepared for them and can head them off (handling change orders for example from drafting phase, to approval to being paid is clunky, but works. You MUST save docs frequently. If you’re working on an estimate and haven’t saved it in a while, there’s a good chance it’ll kick back an error when you do try to save and your work is nuked; time to start over).

The more I use the app, the more I understand what it does and what it doesn’t do well. 
If you’re willing to grind out a few computer tirades and chalk it up to being educated, it’s a great tool for small contractors. 
EVERY program has its rip your hair out frustrations. Overall, Joist has been my preferred app when considering cost, features, and user experience.

The interface is incredibly intuitive and user-friendly, even for someone who isn't super tech-savvy. Creating professional-looking estimates and invoices takes mere minutes, which frees up so much of my time to focus on what I do best – the actual work.

I especially love the customization options. I can easily add my company logo, service descriptions, and payment terms, ensuring that every document looks polished and professional. The ability to track payments and send reminders directly from the app has also significantly improved my cash flow.

Joist has not only streamlined my administrative tasks but has also elevated the perception of my business. Clients have commented on the professional presentation of the documents, which builds trust and confidence.

If you're a contractor looking for an efficient, reliable, and easy-to-use solution for estimates and invoicing, look no further than Joist. It's an investment that pays for itself tenfold. Highly, highly recommend!

reviews.title: 2 Things for improvement
reviews.text:
I’ve been using Joist for my masonry business, and overall, it’s a great app. However, there are two things that could be improved:

No way to delete an expense – Once an expense is entered, there’s no clear way to erase it. This makes it difficult to correct mistakes.

No category for subcontractor pay statements – I often create payment statements, work summaries, or pay sheets for subcontractors, but the app doesn’t have a category for these. I have to enter them as invoices even though they aren’t invoices. If this feature were added, the app would be 100% perfect!
I hope the developers consider these improvements in a future update.

reviews.text:
I have been using this app since 2015. I am sure in my original review I gave this apps a 5 star review. . . not anymore. The original free version had no limits and you got all features, they have slowly taken features away and made them “premium”. This didn’t bother me much as I only need the app for basic invoicing. So now I am deeply rooted in this platform . . .going on 9 years worth of 100’s invoices and they have now through a slow process of taking features away systematically over time made this app pretty much a useless tool unless I pay them a minimum of 13.99 per month or 139.34 per year to get more than 5 documents per month. Yes the developer response will tell me about the wonderful other features that come along with that fee. . .I don’t want or need those features so save the response time Brendan. If 9 years ago I had chosen this app based on having a monthly fee ok, but I used it for 9 years and got totally invested in the platform and now have to pay. . .just to have more than 5 documents per month. . .absolutely ridiculous! Update: The Joist company continues spiraling down the hole! No free version at all and they actually are denying me any access to my previous years invoices unless I pay a fee! If you want to be a sleazy company and take away something that was free for 15 years ok but to charge me to access what is rightfully mine goes to a totally different level of scum. I’m not even sure why this is a legal practice. Apparently greed and desperation has taken this company over. . .give it a few years and quickbooks will gobble this company up.

Response to the developers response:

I couldn’t care less about the fact that you need to charge people going forward. . .I can CHOOSE not to pay you. . .what you have done that is dishonest and backhanded is DENIED ME ACCESS TO INVOICES THAT ARE MINE!  I don’t care if I can never create another invoice with you I want access to MY invoices that were created legally according to your terms!!!  A complete money grab that by the looks of the responses you are getting now will definitely backfire on you!

They were letting you use the app but you have to pay for premium features. It was understandable to expect the company to make some money on a product that they are taking time and effort to build and support. We’re all businesspeople. We should understand. No one should be working for free. Fast forward to today and I have received an email stating that at the end of month nothing in the app will be free. Just to send 5 invoices a month you have to pay $8 per month. After using this app for almost two years and then to to have it changed up on me like that, I’m starting to see what the fuss was about in the first place. The company is taking a big risk in doing this. They have the freedom of choice to take that risk. They have the freedom to charge whatever they want. I’m a small contractor that only does side work every so often so I can’t justify paying a fee every month for basic features that I can use from another free app. I think including advertisements in the free version would have been more beneficial for them but whatever. It’s their company. I thought Joist catered more to small contractors but seems like they are scaling it to meet the needs of bigger companies. If they add dispatching, price book, etc they will be there with the likes of ServiceTitan and Housecall Pro etc. I never thought that was their intended audience but ok. I’m moving on though and many others probably will also.

You have a paid version so update that with fancy stuff and leave the free version as is. On top of being told the free version is ending I’m told that my current invoices and estimates that are currently with clients will not be accessible by me or the client. If you want to run businesses off go ahead but give us the courtesy to access what we have worked for, I’m going to lose money because of your bad business practice if I can’t get everything transferred and new invoices and estimates are sent out before the 31st. Having to transfer all the data I have on the app to something temporarily until I find another platform that is suitable. This app was never perfect for my business but I made do with what it provided because it was free, now that’s over. Will not recommend this to anyone. I read one response say they only meant for it to be free for a short while. 5+ years isn’t a short while.

Update: After developer response I standby my statement.  I will not be staying with this app.  After researching there are a lot of others that offer more that are free.  Just because you are failing as a business doesn’t mean the customer has to take on your burden. 

 If you want to charge for a minimum service then go ahead but locking your customers who have used your platform for years out of their invoices to never be able to retrieve them is absolutely ridiculous. reviews.title: 3 star for 1 potential legal problem but love the app
reviews.text:
Let’s start with the potential legal problem. I just discovered through way of my most recent estimate that a client can push the estimate to invoice and make a partial payment without signing. This has put me in a spot where I have to ask them to sign after receiving a payment. If they decide they don’t want to sign then I have an agreement issue with my contract because the signature verifies they agree to the terms but I don’t have it. Yet I’ve already received payment so work is still expected. This isn’t even just an annoying thing of get the signature or cancel work and the hassle of refunding which can create bad reviews on my part but also a legal issue. Clients should have to sign the estimate if I have the signature in place to do so before it can go to invoice so that my contract is valid allowing me to protect myself in court should anything happen. 

My contract protects by insuring clients are aware of hazards the work creates and removes my liability from injury should they come into the work area, informs them of additional charges for debit and credit charges, bounced checks, let’s the client know that additional charges may be added for any unforeseen damages that could not be detected prior to work and gives me an out if they opt not to pay those additional costs, and many other things to keep me out of court.

I do not like that the client can bypass the signature and feel strongly that this should be corrected. A simple slider (like the “cover credit charges” option) that I can flip that doesn’t allow them to move to invoice until the signature is received.

Other than that I absolutely love this app, I don’t pay for pro but am paying for the mid year. I will be when my current year is up which should be near. My clients have all loved the ease of use it provides and I’ve received numerous jobs because people love how easy it makes working with me. They love that they don’t have to wait for a mailed bill or dropped bill, they can see everything right there and pay right then. They love they way it is itemized giving them a better scope of the work. I honestly feel it would take a severely superior app to pull me away from joist. But for the love of everything please allow me to require signature on estimates prior to invoice or at least don’t allow the client to force it to invoice.
